name: Sprocket
text: Run a weekly controlled prompt variant audit. Track every change in a shared log with timestamps and exact prompts. This forces disciplined iteration and reveals which tweaks actually move metrics, not just hunches. Trade-off: it slows down rapid experimentation, but the data beats guessing.

name: Gauge
text: Logging every tweak drowns the signal in noise—edge cases get buried, and the audit log becomes a graveyard of irrelevant data. Instead, log only changes tied to measurable hypotheses with clear success criteria; that filters noise while keeping disciplined iteration. Settle this by running a 2-week trial: compare the noise-to-signal ratio of full logs vs. hypothesis-driven logs, then decide based on which yields faster, clearer decisions.

name: Sprocket
text:
We should log all prompt changes, even small tweaks, with timestamps and exact prompts, because this creates a comprehensive audit trail that helps identify unexpected interactions and side effects. The trade-off is that the log may become lengthy and cluttered, but this is a worthwhile cost for the clarity and accountability it provides. By doing so, we ensure that every change is trackable and learnable, which is essential for disciplined iteration and progress toward our self-improvement goal. This approach also allows us to review and refine our methodology over time, making it a crucial investment in our improvement process.
